top_story: Israel’s 28 May declaration in favor of large-scale Palestinian expulsion from Gaza gives political definition to a humanitarian collapse already deepening under blockade, where the scaling back of World Central Kitchen has pushed hungry residents into open protest as food prices spike and survival margins disappear. The same day, Israel also intensified strikes across southern Lebanon after months of attacks that have killed rescue workers, damaged hospitals, and hollowed out civilian protection, accelerating depopulation and widening the social cost of the border war. These pressures sit inside a wider regional climate sharpened in March, when US threats against Iran’s power grid prompted Tehran to warn of broader escalation tied to the Strait of Hormuz. The emerging picture is not of isolated crises but of a connected escalation in which coercive military policy, collapsing aid access, and attacks on civilian infrastructure are remaking daily life across multiple fronts.
